title: Faithful morphisms of algebraic stacks are representable by algebraic spaces
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$. Then $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces if and only if, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every two objects $x,x'\in\mathcal X(T)$, the map $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X(T)}(x,x')\to\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y(T)}(F(x),F(x'))$ is injective. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every $2$-base change by an $S$-scheme mapping to $\mathcal Y$ is equivalent over that scheme to an algebraic space regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid.

proof.text: Suppose $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Fix $T$, $x,x'\in\mathcal X(T)$ and arrows $a,b:x\to x'$ with $F(a)=F(b)=\alpha$. In $\mathcal W=h_T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, formed using the object $F(x)$ of $\mathcal Y(T)$, both $a,b$ define arrows $(\mathrm{id}_T,x,\mathrm{id}_{F(x)})\to(\mathrm{id}_T,x',\alpha)$: the compatibility equation is $F(a)\mathrm{id}=\alpha=F(b)\mathrm{id}$. By representability $\mathcal W$ is equivalent to a discrete algebraic-space groupoid, so each of its hom sets has at most one element. Thus these arrows agree and $a=b$.

Conversely assume the stated injectivity for every $S$-scheme. Fix an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$. Regard $h_T$ as a discrete fibred groupoid. It is an algebraic stack: its representing fppf sheaf has effective etale descent (compatible local maps glue uniquely), its diagonal is represented by scheme fibre products, and its identity is a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. The representable smooth calculus makes this atlas smooth, so the definition of algebraic stack applies.

Apply the algebraic-stack fibre-product theorem to $h_T\xrightarrow{y}\mathcal Y\xleftarrow{F}\mathcal X$. All three stacks are algebraic over the same $S$, with no representability assumption on $F$ needed. It follows that $\mathcal W=h_T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack over $S$.

For any $S$-scheme $V$, an object of $\mathcal W(V)$ is $(t:V\to T,x,\alpha:y|_t\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x))$. An arrow to $(t',x',\alpha')$ can exist only if $t=t'$, since $h_T(V)$ is discrete, and is then an arrow $a:x\to x'$ satisfying $F(a)\alpha=\alpha'$. If $a,b$ are two such arrows, cancel the isomorphism $\alpha$ to get $F(a)=F(b)$ and use the assumed injectivity at $V$ to get $a=b$. In particular every automorphism in every fibre of $\mathcal W$ is the identity.

The algebraic-setoid theorem now gives an algebraic space $R/S$ and an equivalence $h_R\simeq\mathcal W$ over $S$. Compose this equivalence with $\mathcal W\to h_T$: since both $h_R$ and $h_T$ are discrete, it is a natural transformation of their sheaves, hence a morphism $R\to T$ by the definition of algebraic-space maps. Equip $R$ with this morphism. The same equivalence is then over $T$; an inverse is over $T$ because its unit and counit become equalities after mapping to the discrete $h_T$. Thus the chosen scheme $2$-base change is an algebraic space over $T$. Since $T,y$ were arbitrary, $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
